1: O God, the shelter of my soul, be Thou the shielding of my body; as Thou art the keeper of the heavens, be Thou the keeper of my going out and my coming in, this day and every day, and in the night when I sleep between Thy hands.

I sit down this night with God, with the Son of God, with the Spirit of grace; I sit down with the Three who never forsake, and the Three who never forsake sit down with me — in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

I will kindle my fire this morning in the presence of the holy angels of heaven, without malice, without jealousy, without envy, without fear — and as the fire of the hearth warms the house, so may the fire of the heart warm the neighbourhood.
2: O God of the sea, put the crew of the boat in Thy protection; give them a clear sky and a favouring wind; bring them home with the harvest of the deep, for the sea is Thy field and the fish are Thy cattle, and the net is the prayer of the poor.

I sow the seed in the furrow of the field, in the name of the Three; and as I sow, I say: the seed is Thine, and the field is Thine, and the harvest is Thine, and the hunger it will answer is Thine also — so let the rain be gentle and the sun be sure.

I milk the cow in the byre this evening, and I say: a blessing on the beast, a blessing on the hand, a blessing on the bowl, and a blessing on the house that the milk will feed — for the little that is blessed is more than the much that is not.
3: The shielding of God be upon you, the covering of the Christ be about you, the mantle of the Spirit be over you, on mountain and on plain, on shore and on sea, on the road that rises and on the road that falls — until the road brings you home.

As the leaf returns to the root, and the wave to the sea, and the ember to the fire, so the soul returns to the God who breathed it. Be not afraid of the going, little soul — the One who made the road has walked it before you.
[Carmina Gadelica III — The mending of the world]

And the old people said: every kindness is a stitch in the torn garment of the world, and every cruelty is a tear; and the garment is being mended, slowly, by hands we cannot see, and our hands are lent to the mending — and that is the whole of the faith of the islands, and it is enough.
